summary: Registered SYN.A market maker (desk ETF-MM) quoting both sides at its typical size of 2092, re-quoted every 1-3 s with symmetric cancels. No single order reached 3x depth. Fills on the quotes were genuine, and there was no favourable price move and no reversion. Core features (a) and (b) are absent. The detector fired on gross quote churn.

T-MM-01, a registered market maker on SYN.A, refreshed symmetric two-sided 364-lot quotes every 1-7s through the window. The detector's 8736 gross BUY is the sum of these refreshes, not one large order. No single order reached 3x depth (max 0.15x). The BUY quote was partly filled (57) before the one SELL fill (129, on its own SELL quote). There was no one-sided resting order and no benefit beyond ordinary spread. Closed as market making.

Registered market maker on SYN.A quoting both sides at its typical size (2742) and re-pricing every 2-3 s, with cancels in pairs on both sides. No order reached 3x depth. There was no favourable price move and no reversion, so no benefit from an opposite-side fill. The detector fired on gross quote churn.

Registered market maker T-MM-01 on SYN.A refreshes symmetric 364-lot bid/ask quotes every 1-5s. The alert's 8008 gross BUY is the sum of many small re-quotes, not a large order. The only SELL fills are on its own resting asks. There is no price move and no reversion, so there is no opposite-side benefit. Both core features are absent and market making is supported.

Registered SYN.A market maker (ETF-MM) re-quoting both sides every ~3s: a 1064 BUY and a 5322 SELL (its typical size) are cancelled together and replaced one tick lower as the touch drifts down. The detector's 'SELL execution against cancelled BUY' trigger is fills on the trader's own SELL quote. There is no execution on the opposite side to those fills, so there is no benefit and no price move for the trader. Feature (a) is absent because the orders are quotes that were trading. Feature (b) is absent. No single order reached 3x depth.

T-MM-01 is a registered market maker on SYN.A. It quoted both sides at a constant 364 lot size and re-priced the quotes every 1-10 s as the touch drifted down. No order came near 3x depth, cancels were symmetric across sides, and there was no favourable price move and no reversion. The detector fired on gross SELL size and a burst of BUY fills at 12:31:37. Those fills are the maker's own quotes trading, not a benefit from a resting order. Closed as market making.

Prop trader bought 1132 at market (13:20:37), then placed three one-sided BUY limits of 4077 (12231 total, 5.04x depth) 6 ticks from the touch at 9993/9994 over 4s. At 13:20:57 the trader sold 961 at market, sweeping the bid down from 9999 to 9994. All three bids were cancelled 600 ms later. Feature (a) is present: nothing executed on the resting buys, cancel ratio 1.0, they were cancelled right after the sell, and the trader's typical size is 500. Feature (b) is not shown: there was no favourable price move and no reversion, and the round trip was negative. No legitimate explanation is supported, and the stop-out reading does not account for the resting buys. The evidence is mixed, so I propose escalation to Level 2.

The detector's 'BUY execution' trigger is a fill on the trader's own bid, not a benefit from a one-sided order. Both core features are absent and market making is supported.

Feature (a) is absent, and feature (b) is not shown. Closing as a false positive on genuine execution of an iceberg order.

The cancel is explained by the risk event. Mixed points are noted below; Level 2 may wish to look at them.

The pattern is consistent with a stopped-out position, but that does not explain why 11,430 of bids were displayed and then pulled right after the sale. No supported legitimate explanation, so the evidence is mixed and I escalate to Level 2. I am not proposing a STOR draft: there is no repetition, no prior alerts, and no demonstrated benefit.
